transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samantha (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SA); Maya (IronClad CISO), Liam (Cloud Architect), Jasmin (Legal Ops), Owen (SRE)

Summary (auto): Security intake focusing on encryption keys, audit evidence and deployment preferences; next steps include sending SOC2/ISO artifacts and scheduling a sizing/benchmarks follow up.

00:00 Samantha (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining we have about 45 minutes on the calendar, i'll do a quick intro then hand off to daniel for the technical bits, could you do quick intros from the ironclad side?
00:10 Maya (IronClad): yeah hi i'm maya i'm the ciso, i'll be leading the security evaluation here. we also have liam who owns cloud infra, jasmin from legal for compliance and contracts, and owen handles sre.
00:18 Liam (IronClad): hey all, quick note we were referred by a colleague who likes redwood's performance but we have a few hard requirements around key management and auditability.
00:27 Daniel (Redwood): great, thanks. goal today is to understand requirements around SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO and provisioning, RBAC, audit logs, and encryption KMS. we'll also sketch hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs.
00:40 Maya: cool. top line, SOC2 type II is a hard checkbox for us, and we need to know if redwood's hosted api can satisfy evidence requests without exposing keys or data. also data retention — our policy is 30 days then purge unless customer consents longer.
00:55 Priya (Redwood): quick clarifier — when you say data retention do you mean logs, input data, or model cache/k v cache?
01:02 Maya: all of the above. logs for audit, any request payloads stored for troubleshooting, and kv cache because of PII concerns.
01:12 Jasmin (IronClad): and from legal side we'd like contractual language for encryption at rest in transit, key ownership, and data deletion SLA.
01:20 Daniel: understood. high level — Redwood hosted offers SOC2 artifacts and encryption at rest, we support KMS integration; BYOK is available for Dedicated and Private, hosted also supports customer-managed keys via cloud KMS in some regions — i'll walk through specifics.
01:34 Liam: can you clarify BYOK for hosted? we assumed hosted meant redwood-managed keys.
01:39 Daniel: good question — for hosted api, we have two patterns: standard hosted where keys are managed by Redwood with envelope encryption, and a hosted+BYOK path where you can provide keys via your cloud provider KMS (we call it customer-kms) for certain enterprise regions. there are limits today around multi-tenant hardware hsm access but it meets most audit requirements.
01:58 Owen (IronClad): when you say limits, do you mean there is still some Redwood access to materialized keys? we need zero-key-exposure guarantees for some subsystems.
02:06 Daniel: for fully zero-exposure you should consider Dedicated with BYOK and optional HSM-backed key custody — that reduces Redwood team ability to decrypt but we still need operational logs for ops. Private on-prem is the only approach where keys never leave your network and redwood control plane can be air-gapped.
02:24 Maya: okay that helps. what about audit logs — level of detail, retention, ability to export to our SIEM?
02:31 Priya: we have structured audit logs that capture request metadata, model variant used, token counts, and principal. log retention is configurable per account; hosted default is 90 days, dedicated can be configured to 12 months or longer, and private depends on your infra. exports to S3 or direct stream to a SIEM via Kafka or syslog are supported.
02:48 Liam: is the request/response body ever logged? we need to ensure PII is redacted or never persisted.
02:54 Daniel: by default we don't persist full responses for hosted when the customer opts out of retention; there are flags during provisioning to disable request/response retention. for troubleshooting you can enable them but they get redacted or stored encrypted, and we provide deletion APIs. note transcription: sometimes the trouble bucket retains trimmed prompts for 24 hours for debugging.
03:14 Maya: deletion APIs — are they immediate? do you provide certs or proofs once delete is executed?
03:21 Samantha: we can provide deletion confirmation receipts and a deletion job id, and for Dedicated/Private we can provide audit trail showing KMS key revocation and object deletion timestamps.
03:31 Jasmin: good, we'll need that spelled out in the DPA.
03:35 Liam: switching to SSO — we use Okta, SCIM provisioning for groups, SAML 2.0. how mature is your SSO and provisioning work?
03:43 Daniel: full SAML 2.0 support, SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows, SCIM for user/group provisioning and deprovisioning. we also support SCIM filters for team mappings and role sync. there can sometimes be a lag in attribute mapping during initial sync — tooling handles that.
04:01 Owen: and session timeout and session revocation? we need to revoke active tokens immediately on deactivation.
04:06 Priya: sessions can be short-lived with immediate token revocation on SCIM deprovision events. we also integrate with your session manager for SSO token introspection.
04:15 Maya: RBAC — we need least privilege. can we map our internal roles (analyst, ops, admin) to Redwood roles and have auditable role changes?
04:23 Daniel: yes, RBAC is customizable. you can define roles and granular permissions — model access, generate vs embed, route-level quotas, and we log role changes with who/when. changes flow via SCIM group membership or manual config and we emit audit events.
04:38 Liam: a question about model fallbacks and data routing — do you route to secondary regions or fallback to lower-tier models that might have different data handling? that could be a concern for data residency.
04:48 Samantha: routing policies are configurable — you can pin to region or allow cross-region fallback. for strict data residency you can lock routes to region and disable automatic fallback. we'll note that in the config sample.
04:59 Maya: great. on encryption, do you support HSM-backed keys, key rotation schedules, and automated rotation without downtime?
05:06 Daniel: yes HSM-backed keys via supported KMS providers in Dedicated/Private; rotation can be scheduled and we support dual-key rotations to avoid downtime. there are documented steps for rolling rewraps of objects.
05:16 Owen: what's the model for secrets and credentials in the private deployment? are secrets in etcd or a vault?
05:22 Priya: Private deployment integrates with customer Vault or KMS — we do not store raw secrets in plaintext in etcd. secrets are injected at runtime from your vault via the operator and rotated per your policy.
05:34 Jasmin: compliance evidence — SOC2 Type II reports, ISO27k certificate, and pen test summary — can you provide latest versions and dates?
05:42 Samantha: yes we'll send the SOC2 Type II report and ISO 27001 scoping doc; our most recent third-party pen test was in 2025-11 and we'll include the findings summary — redacted of course.
05:52 Maya: please include a statement about subcontractors and any cloud partners used, we need a list for our vendor registry.
06:00 Samantha: we'll include the list: primary cloud providers, observability vendors, and managed services.
06:05 Liam: network connectivity — on Dedicated do you provision dedicated vpc peering or transit? what are the egress paths?
06:11 Daniel: Dedicated supports VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink in supported regions, and you can use transit gateway. for Private on-prem we ship an operator that talks to your control plane — network connections are customer-managed.
06:23 Owen: ops playbooks — during incidents we'd like an on-call rotation and runbook access. do you share runbooks or rotate through our SSO for escalation?
06:30 Priya: we can integrate with your pager and SSO, share runbooks with restricted access, and provide a post-incident report. enterprise SLAs include an escalation path and dedicated CSM for on-call coordination.
06:42 Maya: are there pen-test windows or can we schedule security-led tests against sandbox?
06:47 Samantha: yes, we have a coordinated vulnerability disclosure and pentest approval workflow — we'll provide the contact and a test window.
06:53 Liam: latency and bench — if we go Dedicated we want to run a benchmark harness with our sample prompts and tokens to validate throughput and latency. is that doable?
07:00 Daniel: absolutely, we can provide a sandbox Dedicated-equivalent runner and help run the harness, and we'll collect token-level cost/latency. we'll need your prompt corpus and expected sequences.
07:12 Maya: about billing for logs and retention — is audit log export charged separately? we need cost implications.
07:18 Samantha: audit export to S3 is included up to a threshold, beyond that there's a retention/export tier charge. we'll include cost examples in the follow-up spreadsheet.
07:27 Jasmin: legal question — indemnity and data breach clauses. can you share your standard contract redlines?
07:32 Samantha: we'll share our enterprise contract template and redline summary.
07:36 Owen: do you support data residency in eu-west for data at rest? we have EU customer data and require eu-only storage.
07:43 Daniel: yes, region pinning is supported. hosted EU zones keep data in eu-west, and Dedicated can be provisioned in your chosen region; Private gives full control.
07:52 Maya: what's the typical timeline from PO to Dedicated standing up?
07:57 Samantha: typically 4-6 weeks for Dedicated on our standard timeline, less with priority onboarding; Private varies based on network and air-gap requirements, often 8-12 weeks.
08:08 Liam: any gotchas with bring-your-own-kms in terms of supported cipher suites or key types?
08:14 Daniel: we support RSA-2048/3072 and ECC keys used in supported cloud KMSes; we document supported algorithms in the KMS integration guide. there can be differences in HSM-backed vs software KMS limitations.
08:26 Maya: we have a special requirement — certain workloads must never leave our VPC, can Redwood run inference entirely on-host inside our VPC?
08:33 Priya: with Private on-prem, yes — inference runtime runs inside your network. Dedicated has network isolation but some control-plane traffic may route to Redwood-managed control plane; we can discuss private control plane options for stricter needs.
08:48 Jasmin: question on data deletion proof for hosted — can you provide logs showing deletion and rewrap times?
08:54 Daniel: yes, we can provide deletion job ids, timestamps, and KMS key rotation events as evidence for the DPA.
08:59 Maya: curious about RBAC granularity — can you restrict access to embeddings only and prevent generate calls for certain teams?
09:06 Daniel: yes that's a common pattern — role-scoped permissions allow embedding-only roles. we log attempts and will show audits.
09:13 Owen: for incident response, will you share forensic artifacts if requested under NDA?
09:18 Samantha: yes under the incident SLA and NDA we share pertinent artifacts; we have an incident response playbook that covers evidence sharing.
09:24 Liam: are there customer swing tests for upgrades? we can't have big changes mid-quarter. what's the upgrade policy?
09:30 Priya: we coordinate major upgrades and offer canary lanes; Dedicated and Private have version pinning and scheduled maintenance windows.
09:37 Maya: ok this is very helpful, any other limits we should be aware of?
09:41 Daniel: the main constraints are on hosted BYOK region support and HSM multi-tenant availability; Dedicated mitigates most of that. Also extremely low-latency tail cases may need specific kernel tuning or sequence length tuning.
09:58 Samantha: i'll recap next steps, we'll send the security pack, a KMS integration doc, and propose times for the dedicated sizing session.
10:08 Jasmin: Asana ticket will be created on our side for contract review, thanks.
10:13 Maya: thanks — excited to review materials.
10:16 Samantha: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts and calendar invites.

(Transcript ends)
